name: n4_alarm_health
description: How healthy the station's alarms are, in one call. A source stored as slot:/a or local:|station:|slot:/a is reported once as station:|slot:/a (the form the source filter of n4_read_alarms and n4_event_report takes). chattering (sources with at least chatter_threshold transitions in the window, most first, as {source, transitions, records}; each alarm record whose alarm time is in the window counts one transition out of normal, plus one back when its normal time is set), offnormal (sources with an open record not back to normal, once per source, oldest first, as {source, source_state, alarm_class, since, records}: since, state and class of its earliest such record), unacked_older (records not acknowledged whose alarm time is more than unacked_days days old, oldest first, as {source, alarm_class, ack_state, alarm_time, age_days}) and top_sources (every source of the window by record count, most first, as {source, count}). Each list is cut to top entries; counts gives the full numbers, truncated is true and truncated_note says which lists were cut or which read stopped at its 100000-record cap. window is a span back from now such as 30m, 24h or 7d. Read-only: two fixed BQL reads of the alarm: ORD (select source, normalTime.encodeToString where timestamp.millis >= <window start>; select source, sourceState.encodeToString, ackState.encodeToString, alarmClass, timestamp.encodeToString over the open records), grouped by the server; never a write. To act on a finding, read its events with n4_event_report or n4_read_alarms.

window.description: Span back from now the chattering and top-source counts cover: 1 to 5 digits and m, h or d, e.g. 30m, 24h, 7d

chatter_threshold.description: Transitions in the window from which a source counts as chattering

unacked_days.description: Age in days beyond which (strictly more than) an unacknowledged alarm is listed in unacked_older

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds
